headlines.title: 종전 합의에 국제유가 3∼ 4% 급락 …국내 반영 언제쯤?

headlines.title: 반도체만 영업익 961% ↑…‘ K자 양극화 ’ 2분기 더 심해진다

headlines.summary: 5월 1674만명… 1년새 7000명↓ 2030은 팬데믹 후 최대폭 감소 고용안정성이 높은 상용근로자가 26년 5개월 만에 처음으로 감소했다. 특히 20·30대 상용근로자는 코로나19 팬데믹 이후 가장 큰 폭으로 줄었다. 반도체를 제외한 나머지 제조업 부진이 심화하는 K자형 경제 흐름이 20·30대 일자리에 타격을 주고 있는 것이다.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's May Exports Hit Record 87.8 Billion Dollars Driven by Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: South Korea achieved record monthly exports of 87.8 billion dollars in May, with semiconductor exports surging 167.7% year-on-year, maintaining 12 consecutive months of export growth and posting 27 billion dollars in trade surplus.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Surges 5% as US-Iran War Peace Deal Signals Economic Relief
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index jumped 5% in early trading following news of a US-Iran peace agreement, with WTI crude oil prices stabilizing around 80 dollars per barrel, easing geopolitical tensions affecting Korean markets.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Sector Operating Profit Surges 961% amid K-Shaped Economic Polarization
key_headlines.summary: Top 30 companies are projected to earn 175 trillion won in Q2 operating profits, with semiconductor firms (Samsung, SK Hynix, Hanmi) accounting for 84% (148 trillion won), while 27 non-semiconductor companies face declining profits, deepening Korea's K-shaped economic divide.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Japan and Fed Rate Decisions Loom as Key Economic Variables Next Week
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to raise its policy rate from 0.75% to 1.0% on June 16, while Fed Chair Kevin Wash will chair his first FOMC meeting on June 18, with potential rate decisions becoming critical market drivers.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Average Home Price Exceeds 1 Billion Won as Property Market Reaches New Heights
key_headlines.summary: Seoul's average housing price surpassed 1 billion won in May 2026, with Gyeonggi Province also recording triple highs across sales, lease, and jeonse (long-term deposit rental) markets, driven by strong demand for new construction and reconstruction projects.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's export sector is experiencing exceptional momentum with May exports reaching a record 87.8 billion dollars, driven primarily by a remarkable 167.7% surge in semiconductor exports. The country has maintained 12 consecutive months of export growth, with the semiconductor sector's operating profit projected to jump 961% in Q2, creating a stark K-shaped economic pattern where chip companies dominate while other industries struggle. Geopolitical relief from the US-Iran peace agreement has boosted market sentiment, with the KOSPI jumping 5% and crude oil prices stabilizing around 80 dollars per barrel, easing previous concerns about inflation and supply chain disruptions.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea is projected to accelerate its rate-hiking cycle, with analysts predicting the benchmark rate could reach 4.0% by next year if the central bank raises rates consecutively in the second half, up from current expectations of 3.5%. Margin firms are creating negative externalities on healthy companies, with research showing that a 1 percentage point increase in marginal firm share reduces normal firm investment and employment growth by up to 0.18 percentage points, highlighting the need for improved market exit mechanisms. The government is considering ending price caps on petroleum products following the Middle East peace resolution, though refineries and petrochemical companies face near-term inventory losses from reverse lag effects before achieving mid-to-long-term cost stabilization.
sections.Financial Markets: Foreign investors have become net sellers of Korean equities with record outflows of 70.2 billion dollars in May, despite purchasing 8.5 trillion won of Korean bonds as US Treasury yields rose amid inflation concerns and anticipated central bank rate hikes. The KOSPI recovered to over 8,500 points, gaining 5.2%, while the KOSDAQ rose 1.86%, with the won strengthening to 1,514.40 per dollar as geopolitical tensions eased following the US-Iran ceasefire agreement. Market participants are closely watching the Bank of Japan's June 16 rate decision and the Fed's June 18 FOMC meeting, as these central bank actions are expected to be critical variables determining Korean stock market direction alongside semiconductor earnings results.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery and semiconductor industries are intensifying competition with China in emerging sectors, particularly in electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft batteries as both nations eye the future urban air mobility market. Domestic companies including Shinsung E&G are partnering internationally, such as with India's Sterling and Wilson, to develop advanced HVAC systems for semiconductor fabs, battery plants, and display factories across Asia. The biotech sector is advancing with innovations in Alzheimer's disease treatment strategies and blood-based diagnostics, while the government's Biotech Innovation Committee is strengthening collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to enhance global competitiveness and build a robust innovation ecosystem.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's housing market has reached a new milestone with average property prices exceeding 1 billion won in May 2026, while Gyeonggi Province simultaneously hit record highs across sales, lease, and jeonse categories driven by strong demand for newly built and reconstructed apartment complexes. Investor interest is shifting toward older properties in major Chinese cities where modest 2-3% rental yields exceed traditional investment products returning only 1%, reflecting changing investment strategies amid prolonged property slumps. Secondary cities near Seoul such as Dongtan, Suji, and Giheung are experiencing heated competition as investment demand spreads, with Giheung crossing the 1.5 billion won national average price threshold for premium complexes near Samsung and SK Hynix semiconductor facilities.
sections.International Economy: US President Trump has threatened 100% tariffs on French wine and champagne unless France abolishes its digital services tax, continuing his administration's aggressive trade strategy against what it views as discriminatory taxation of American technology companies. Fed Chair Kevin Wash faces a policy dilemma between his past hawkish positions favoring rate increases and the Trump administration's preference for rate cuts, creating uncertainty about the central bank's upcoming June 18 FOMC decision and its impact on global markets. The international trade environment remains tense, with Canada having already withdrawn its digital services tax proposal and Italy considering similar moves, as Trump uses tariff threats to reshape global trade policies in line with US interests.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korea and Japan have launched formal economic cooperation frameworks to strengthen AI-related industrial collaboration, focusing on power efficiency in AI infrastructure and care robotics development to address shared societal challenges and maintain global competitiveness. EdgeAI companies are attracting investor attention as AI datacenters emerge as critical infrastructure, with Korean firms positioning themselves to lead in this high-growth market sector alongside traditional industrial transformation efforts. However, concerns are mounting about AI's displacement of skilled workers, with salaried employment declining for the first time in 26 years and workers aged 20-30 experiencing significant job losses in IT, professional, scientific, and technology services, raising questions about whether AI advancement will create sufficient new opportunities to offset displaced workers.
sections.Others: China's rapid AI and automation adoption is transforming production processes and replacing human labor across industries, even as the country grapples with persistently high youth unemployment, creating a paradox where technological advancement coincides with workforce displacement challenges.
